channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: South Korean Won: Weak KRW and hawkish BoK expectations – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank highlights strong South Korean export momentum, led by semiconductors and petroleum, but notes that South Korean Won (KRW) remains one of Asia’s weakest currencies versus the Dollar.

item.title: Australian Dollar nears three-month low ahead of Australian CPI data
item.description: The AUD/USD fell sharply near the 0.6920 level on Tuesday, as investors await the upcoming Australian Consumer Price Index (CPI) release for fresh clues on the Reserve Bank of Australia’s (RBA) policy outlook.

item.title: Dow Jones Industrial Average green by default as chips crater
item.description: The Dow Jones Industrial Average (DJIA) held in the green through Tuesday even as the rest of the equity board bled. On the surface that reads as strength; underneath, it is anything but. The index held up for the least flattering reason on offer, namely its composition.

item.title: India: Interim US trade deal and tariff landscape – DBS
item.description: DBS economist Radhika Rao reports that India and US are close to formalising an interim trade agreement under a new framework first agreed in February.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Steadies as USD/JPY rally tires – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret report the Japanese Yen (JPY) is slightly firmer, outperforming G10 peers despite broad US Dollar (USD) strength, as stronger PMIs signal improving growth. They see signs of exhaustion in USD/JPY’s advance with yield spreads stabilizing.

item.title: WTI Oil retreats as lower Middle East risk, Iran supply return weigh on prices
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) US Oil declines by more than 1% on Tuesday and trades around $73.00 at the time of writing, pressured as traders continue to assess diplomatic developments between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: Euro stabilizes against British Pound as weak UK PMIs contrast with resilient Eurozone activity
item.description: EUR/GBP trades little changed on Tuesday after a sharp slide the previous day, triggered by UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer's resignation, which lifted the British Pound (GBP) across the board.

item.title: Japanese Yen trades in neutral zone as investors assess US PMIs and ADP data
item.description: The USD/JPY pair is trading in a neutral zone on Tuesday as investors digest the latest United States (US) Purchasing Managers Index (PMI) figures and recent ADP employment data, awaiting a stronger catalyst from Federal Reserve (Fed) commentary.

item.title: British Pound falls amid UK political uncertainty and hot US PMI
item.description: The Pound Sterling (GBP) dives over 0.40% on Tuesday as risk appetite shifts sour, as the recently sworn-in MP Andy Burnham prepares to succeed Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who lasted two years at the job. At the time of writing, GBP/USD trades at 1.3195, after reaching a daily high of 1.3257.

item.title: Gold languishes near $4,100 as US Dollar hits one-year highs, PMIs beat forecasts
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trades on the back foot on Tuesday, pressured by a stronger US Dollar (USD) and rising expectations that the Federal Reserve (Fed) could raise interest rates later this year.

item.title: Reserve Bank of Australia: Slowing demand supports steady rates – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities strategist Prashant Newnaha notes that softer S&P Australia Flash Composite PMI data, including weaker new orders and moderating price pressures, supports the Reserve Bank of Australia keeping its cash rate unchanged at 4.35% in August.

item.title: Canadian Dollar falls to multi‑month low as Fed hike bets rise, Oil weighs
item.description: USD/CAD trades around 1.4190 on Tuesday at the time of writing, up 0.25% on the day and extending a four-day winning streak to its highest level since April 7.

item.title: Euro drops below 1.1400 as hawkish Fed bets push the US Dollar to one-year highs
item.description: The Euro (EUR) extends losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Tuesday, with EUR/USD slipping below the 1.1400 mark, a support level that had held since June 2025.

item.title: Natural gas: Lower TTF path but winter risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s energy strategists Joe DeLaura and Florence Schmit cut TTF Natural Gas forecasts on easing supply risks from the Strait of Hormuz reopening.

item.title: Euro area: PMIs signal weak activity and sticky prices – Nomura
item.description: Nomura strategists note Euro area business activity stayed in contraction in June, with the composite PMI at 49.5 despite a small rise.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal worries cap recovery against US Dollar – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the British Pound (GBP) is softer versus the US Dollar (USD) after mildly disappointing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) and CBI data, with market reaction muted.

item.title: Oil: Limited downside as sanctions ease – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Carsten Fritsch notes that Brent has dropped back below USD 80, briefly touching USD 76.5, after the US allowed Iran to export oil and oil products until at least August 21.

item.title: Copper: Tariff support versus demand risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ commodity team notes that Copper is seeing large CTA (Commodity Trading Advisors) selling as markets look past Strait of Hormuz supply risks and focus more on macro and demand-side weakness.

item.title: BoE’s Taylor: “We enter this shock with a very weak economy”
item.description: Bank of England (BoE) policymaker Alan Taylor said on Tuesday that keeping interest rates on hold for an extended period remains the most appropriate policy response, according to the text of a speech due to be delivered at an event hosted by Barclays and the Center for Economic Policy Research.

item.title: “Global imbalances are growing and may also be fuelling financial stability risks”: BoC's Macklem
item.description: Bank of Canada (BoC) Governor Tiff Macklem said on Tuesday that global imbalances are increasing and may risk financial stability.

item.title: Breaking: United States S&P Global Composite PMI improves to 52.2 in June
item.description: The flash estimate of the United States (US) S&P Global Composite PMI came in at 52.2 in June, better than the 51.5 posted in May.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Remains soft as USD trend extends – Scotiabank
item.description: Scotiabank strategists Shaun Osborne and Eric Theoret note the Canadian Dollar (CAD) retains a soft undertone despite a first modest gain versus the US Dollar (USD) in eight sessions, helped by firmer May Consumer Price Index (CPI) and steadier US–Canada spreads.

item.title: Oil: Sanctions waiver pressures prices – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey say Oil prices fell sharply after the US granted a 60-day waiver allowing Iranian exports, adding to pressure from rising flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: Can bulls defend $60 as the US Dollar climbs to one-year highs?
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) slides more than 4% on Tuesday as the US Dollar (USD) climbs to near one-year highs after the Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish tilt at last week's monetary policy meeting reinforced expectations that interest rates will remain higher for longer.

item.title: Euro: Eurozone PMIs show two-speed recovery – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Global Strategy Team reports that June Eurozone PMIs confirm a divergence between stabilizing German manufacturing and still weak French services.

item.title: Fed: Warsh era keeps markets guessing – NBC
item.description: National Bank of Canada (NBC) Economics and Strategy team, led by Taylor Schleich, Ethan Currie and Vy Le, argues that Kevin Warsh’s Federal Reserve (Fed) is deliberately increasing policy ambiguity by stripping out forward guidance.

item.title: Euro: Softer PMIs challenge ECB tightening case – BNY
item.description: Geoff Yu at BNY highlights that Eurozone PMIs remain weak despite a slightly better-than-expected composite reading. Core economies like Germany and France continue to underperform, with German services at a 43‑month low.

item.title: Natural gas: Heat and outages support prices – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank analysts highlight that stronger heatwaves in Europe and Asia are likely to lift electricity demand and gas-fired power use, complicating European storage refilling.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Breakout risks build on hawkish Fed – OCBC
item.description: OCBC’s Sim Moh Siong notes the Dollar is supported by higher US Treasury yields and a more hawkish Federal Reserve path, with leaner Fed communication likely to lift FX volatility.

item.title: United States ADP Employment Change 4-week average increases to 30.75K
item.description: Private-sector hiring in the US has increased in early June. According to the NER Pulse, the weekly companion to the ADP National Employment Report, companies added an average of 30.75K jobs per week in the four weeks ending June 6.
